items.defectStatement: The team authorization expression requires both admin and owner checks to succeed. A team admin who is neither the organizer nor an attendee is therefore incorrectly rejected with FORBIDDEN.
obligations: Authorize either an admin or an owner of the booking's team.
Continue rejecting users who satisfy none of the authorized roles.
items.notes: isTeamAdmin already accepts owners in this repository; using OR remains correct and is supported by the frozen input.

items.defectStatement: The input schema accepts repeated email strings, and the handler only filters against previously stored attendees. Repeating a new email within one request therefore produces duplicate attendee rows.
obligations: Prevent repeated email strings in one request from producing multiple attendee rows.
Preserve email-format validation and numeric bookingId validation.
Continue accepting requests containing distinct valid emails.
items.notes: Rejecting duplicate inputs with a refinement is also valid. Case-insensitive uniqueness is addressed separately by kimi-01.

items.defectStatement: The guest filter compares raw email strings against existing attendees and a lowercased blacklist, allowing case variants of existing or blacklisted addresses through. It also permits differently cased copies of the same new address within one request.
obligations: Exclude existing attendees using case-insensitive email comparison.
Exclude blacklisted addresses regardless of input casing.
Accept at most one case-insensitive occurrence of each new email per request.
Preserve accepted email spelling so downstream exact-match email classification still recognizes new attendees.
items.notes: Normalize comparison keys while retaining accepted input strings. Lowercasing stored guest values alone can break the unchanged sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) call's exact-match classification.

items.defectStatement: The add-guests handler compares raw guest addresses against lowercased blacklist entries, allowing case variants and plus-address aliases of blocked addresses to become attendees and receive invitations. Unlike handleNewBooking, it does not normalize incoming guests to lowercase base addresses before checking the blacklist.
obligations: Exclude guests whose lowercase base address matches a lowercased blacklist entry, including case variants and plus-address aliases.
Preserve existing-attendee exclusion and retain the submitted email addresses for allowed guests.
Preserve empty-blacklist behavior and the existing error when no eligible guests remain.
items.notes: The replacement deliberately leaves the filter's closing `);` on line 78 untouched. extractBaseEmail is not imported; equivalent inline normalization keeps the fix within the anchor. Lowercasing alone leaves the finding's plus-alias bypass unresolved.

items.defectStatement: The handler passes raw request guests to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the filtered guests actually added. Existing attendees included in a successful request consequently receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.
obligations: Classify only the newly added, filtered guests as new email recipients.
Preserve the full event attendee list so existing attendees still receive add-guests notifications.
items.notes: A rejected blacklisted address receives no email unless it already appears among event attendees. uniqueGuests excludes existing attendees and blacklisted addresses but does not deduplicate repeated request entries.
